A harder, brighter pluck, closer to a steel-string guitar.
Short, muted notes, like a string damped with the palm.

sounds.name: Slow-Swept Distorted Riff
sounds.ref: In the style of Daft Punk — "Rock’n Roll"
sounds.blurb: A gritty, heavily distorted low riff whose filter slowly opens and closes by itself over several bars.
sounds.how: A sawtooth and a pulse, a few cents apart, give a thick, rough tone in the bass register. The low-pass filter rests low, and one cable sends the upward-only LFO into FREQ MOD, so a slow triangle lifts the cutoff and lets it fall back about every nine seconds without you touching anything. Heavy overdrive comes after the filter: while the filter is shut the riff is a dark growl, and as it opens the distortion turns it into a harsh buzz.

steps.title: A sawtooth and a pulse together
steps.why:
A sawtooth and a pulse, slightly apart, give a thick, rough bass tone. The slow beating between them makes it fatter than either oscillator alone.
- SHAPE osc 1 2 (saw), SHAPE osc 2 1 (pulse), WIDTH osc 2 3 (32%): a buzzy saw and a narrower, nasal pulse.
- RANGE 16’ on both: an octave below normal, in the bass register.
- TUNE osc 2 +0.1 st: about 12 cents sharp, which gives the slow beating.
- OSC MIX 0 (50 / 50): an equal blend on the crossfader.
- Listen for: hold a low note and hear the slow wobble between the two.

steps.title: A low filter with a short bite
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) rests low so the riff is dark, with a small bite from Envelope 2 to keep the rhythm clear.
- MODE low-pass, FREQ 4.2 (about 220 Hz): the darkest point. Raise it and the riff never gets fully muffled.
- RESO 5: resonance puts a peak on the cutoff, which the sweep and overdrive will exaggerate.
- KEY TRK off: the cutoff stays put across the riff.
- ENV DEPTH 2.5 with Envelope 2 A 0, D 150 ms, S 20%: a quick lift at the front of each note.
- Listen for: a dark, muffled riff with a small click of brightness on each note.

steps.title: Patch LFO UNI → FREQ MOD
steps.why:
The LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves other settings) normally swings the cutoff both ways. The upward-only version makes FREQ the floor, so the LFO only ever opens the filter.
- LFO UNI → FREQ MOD: replaces the normal LFO feed with the one that only rises from zero.
- MOD DEPTH 5 (50%): up to about two and a half octaves of opening. At 0 the riff stays dark; at 10 it goes from growl to scream every cycle.
- Listen for: the tone brightening and darkening by itself. It is still at the default LFO speed, so it moves quickly for now.

steps.title: A slow triangle LFO
steps.why:
Slowing the LFO turns the fast wobble into a sweep over several bars.
- SHAPE 1 (triangle): opens and closes at the same speed. A saw would open slowly and snap shut.
- RATE 1.5 (0.11 Hz): about nine seconds per cycle. Around 3 it becomes a wah on every bar.
- KEY SYNC off: the sweep runs free across notes instead of restarting.
- Listen for: hold a note. The filter opens over four or five seconds and closes over the same time.

steps.title: Heavy overdrive and tight notes
steps.why:
Heavy overdrive after the filter makes the sweep change the grit: dark notes growl, bright ones rasp. Envelope 1 on the VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) keeps the stabs tight.
- DRIVE 8.5: most of the grit. Turn it down to 2 to hear the plain swept sound underneath.
- TONE 6.5: right of centre for a harder edge.
- LEVEL 5: down, because heavy drive is loud.
- Envelope 1 A 0, D 150 ms, S 80%, R 12 ms: an instant start and a very short release, so notes stop cleanly.
- PORTA TIME 0: no slides; notes step.
- Listen for: the riff going from a muffled growl to a harsh buzz and back as the sweep moves.

context.vcf.modDepth: In this sound it sets how far the LFO sweep opens the filter. At 0 the riff stays dark all the time; at 10 it goes from a growl to a scream every cycle.
context.lfo.rate: The speed of the sweep, about nine seconds per cycle. Around 3 it becomes a steady wah on every bar.
context.lfo.shape: Triangle opens and closes at the same speed. Sawtooth would open slowly and snap shut.
context.vcf.freq: The darkest point of the sweep. Raise it and the riff never gets fully muffled.
context.vcf.reso: Puts a peak on the sweep. The overdrive makes that peak sound harsher.
context.od.drive: Most of the grit. Turn it down to 2 to hear the plain swept sound underneath.
context.od.level: Turned down to make up for how loud heavy drive is.
context.osc2.tune: About 12 cents sharp of Oscillator 1. The slow beating is what makes the tone thick.
context.vcf.envDepth: The small bite at the front of each note.

tweaks.hear: The sweep speeds up to about one cycle a second and the riff gets a regular wah.
From a gentle brightening to a full sweep from growl to scream.

tweaks.try: Pull back to 2, then return to 8.5
tweaks.hear: First a clean, filtered riff, then the same riff torn up. The sweep is much easier to hear with the drive on.

sounds.name: Bright Gliding Echo Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Kraftwerk — "Spacelab"
sounds.blurb: A bright, clean lead that slides from note to note, with a slight vibrato and soft echoes behind it.
sounds.how: Two sawtooths, one a few cents sharp, make a bright, full tone, and the filter stays mostly open and follows the keys. PORTA TIME makes every note slide up or down to the next, so wide jumps become smooth sweeps. A cable sends the LFO, turned down by Attenuator 2, to the pitch of both oscillators for a slight vibrato, and a quiet delay timed to eighth notes adds a sense of space.

steps.title: Two bright sawtooths
steps.why:
Two sawtooths, one a little sharp, give a bright, full lead that sounds like one thick voice rather than two notes.
- SHAPE 2 (saw) and RANGE 8’ on both: every harmonic, so it is bright and cuts through.
- TUNE osc 2 +0.1 st: about 10 cents sharp. The slow beating thickens the tone.
- OSC MIX 0 (50 / 50): an equal blend on the crossfader.
- Listen for: a bright, buzzy lead with a slow shimmer.

steps.title: An open filter that follows the keys
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) stays mostly open and follows the keys, with a small lift from Envelope 2 at the start of each note.
- MODE low-pass, FREQ 7.2 (about 1.9 kHz): how bright the lead is. Below about 6 it turns soft and flute-like.
- RESO 2.5: resonance, a little edge at the cutoff.
- KEY TRK on: key tracking keeps the high notes as bright as the low ones.
- ENV DEPTH 1.5 with Envelope 2 A 0, D 360 ms, S 50%: a slightly brighter start that settles in about a third of a second.
- Listen for: each note starting a touch brighter than it holds.

steps.title: Slide between every note
steps.why:
Portamento is the main character of this lead: every note slides to the next.
- PORTA TIME 1.5 (220 ms): about a quarter of a second to reach each new note. At 0 notes step; above about 3 every note is a long, slow swoop.
- Listen for: the jumps in the riff sweeping up or down instead of stepping.

steps.title: Patch ATT 2 → OSC 1+2 for vibrato
steps.why:
Attenuator 2 already carries the LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves other settings). This cable sends it to both oscillators’ pitch for a slight vibrato.
- ATT 2 → OSC 1+2: the LFO to both pitches. The pulse-width feed does nothing here, as sawtooths have no pulse width.
- 2 at 0.8: about a third of a semitone. Even 2 gives a wide, wobbly pitch.
- RATE 4.9 (5.64 Hz), SHAPE sine, KEY SYNC off: a smooth vibrato of about 5.5 Hz, free-running.
- Listen for: held notes wavering gently.

steps.title: Loudness and a quiet echo
steps.why:
Envelope 1 shapes loudness through the VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier), and a timed echo adds space behind the lead.
- Envelope 1 A 1 ms, S 100%, R 140 ms: full level straight away, and a brief fade into the next slide.
- TIME 7.1 (250 ms): an eighth note at 120 bpm.
- REPEATS 35%, MIX 2.5 (25%): a few quiet echoes that add space without extra notes.
- DRIVE 0.5: nearly clean.
- Listen for: echoes sitting in time behind the lead without blurring it.

context.porta.time: In this sound the glide is the main character. At 0 the notes step; above about 3 every note is a long, slow swoop.
context.att.2: The vibrato depth, through the cable to OSC 1+2. Even 2 gives a wide, wobbly pitch; keep it small.
context.lfo.rate: The vibrato speed, about 5.5 Hz.
context.vcf.freq: How bright the lead is. Below about 6 it turns soft and flute-like.
context.vcf.keyTrk: Keeps the high notes of the riff as bright as the low ones.
context.osc2.tune: About 10 cents sharp. The slow beating between the two sawtooths thickens the tone.
context.delay.mix: How loud the echoes are. Kept low so they add space rather than extra notes.
context.delay.time: 250 ms, an eighth note at 120 bpm.
context.env1.r: About 140 ms, so each note fades briefly into the next slide.

tweaks.hear: From plain stepped notes to long sweeps where the pitch is still moving when the next note starts.
The echoes become a trail of notes behind the lead and the sound feels much further away.
An octave below joins the lead and it becomes fuller and more organ-like.

sounds.name: Gliding Sync Yelp Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Bernie Worrell — "Bop Gun (Endangered Species)" (Parliament, "Funkentelechy vs. the Placebo Syndrome")
sounds.blurb: A high, rubbery funk lead that slides between notes and gives a squelchy "yow" at the start of each one.
sounds.how: P-Funk synth leads slide, squeal and bend like a voice clowning around. Here Oscillator 2 is hard-synced to Oscillator 1, so its pitch knob changes the tone instead of the pitch. Envelope 2 is patched through Attenuator 1 into Oscillator 2’s pitch, so at the start of each note the synced tone jumps up and then falls back as the envelope decays: a "yow" that sounds like a vowel changing. The same envelope opens a resonant filter, and PORTA TIME slides every note into the next.

steps.title: Two sawtooths with OSC SYNC on
steps.why:
OSC SYNC (hard sync) makes Oscillator 2 restart on every cycle of Oscillator 1, so it plays Oscillator 1’s pitch and its TUNE knob changes the tone instead of the note.
- SHAPE 2 (saw), RANGE 8’ on both: sawtooths give the strongest sync edge.
- TUNE osc 2 1.2 (+2.9 st): with sync on, a brighter, slightly hollow tone rather than a different note. Higher is more nasal.
- OSC SYNC on: switch it off and Oscillator 2 plays a separate, clashing note.
- OSC MIX 2 (30 / 70): the crossfader leans towards the synced oscillator, so it does most of the talking.
- Listen for: a bright, nasal lead at the pitch you play.

steps.title: A resonant filter that opens on each note
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) gets a resonant squelch from Envelope 2 on every note.
- MODE low-pass, FREQ 6.8 (about 1.4 kHz): the resting tone.
- RESO 4.5: resonance gives the filter movement its squelch.
- KEY TRK on: key tracking keeps high notes as bright as low ones.
- ENV DEPTH 2.5 with Envelope 2 A 0, D 360 ms, S 25%: opens by about two octaves and falls back over a third of a second.
- Listen for: a “wow” of brightness at the start of each note.

steps.title: Patch ENV 2 → ATT1 IN and ATT 1 → OSC 2
steps.why:
The patch bay adds the yelp. Envelope 2 goes to Oscillator 2’s pitch, and because sync is on, that sweeps the tone rather than the note.
- ENV 2 → ATT1 IN: Envelope 2 replaces Attenuator 1’s usual input.
- ATT 1 → OSC 2: adds it to Oscillator 2’s pitch.
- 1 at 5: about an octave of lift at the start of each note, falling back as Envelope 2 decays. This is the size of the “yow”.
- Listen for: a vowel-like “yow” on every note. Envelope 2 drives both this and the filter, so both move together.

steps.title: Slides between notes
steps.why:
Portamento slides every note into the next, which makes the line playful and voice-like.
- PORTA TIME 1.6 (260 ms): about a quarter of a second per slide. The riff has wide jumps, so this is easy to hear.
- Listen for: rubbery slides up and down between notes, each ending in a “yow”.

steps.title: Loudness, grit and a short echo
steps.why:
Envelope 1 sets loudness through the VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier). The overdrive fattens the synced tone, and a short echo adds a little room.
- Envelope 1 A 0.5 (near 0 ms), D 360 ms, S 80%, R 63 ms: an instant start, held notes stay loud, and a quick stop.
- DRIVE 3, TONE 5.5, LEVEL 7.5: some grit, slightly bright.
- TIME 6 (170 ms), REPEATS 30%, MIX 1.5 (15%): a short, quiet echo.
- Listen for: a fuller, slightly gritty lead with a small room behind it.

context.att.1: In this sound this is the size of the "yow": how far Envelope 2 pushes the synced Oscillator 2 up at the start of each note. At 5 it is about an octave.
context.osc.sync: Makes Oscillator 2 follow Oscillator 1’s pitch, so the envelope on Oscillator 2 changes the tone rather than the note. Turn it off and each note starts with a pitch jump on Oscillator 2 instead.
context.osc2.tune: The resting tone of the synced oscillator. Higher is more nasal and cutting.
context.env2.d: The length of the "yow" and of the filter’s squelch, because Envelope 2 drives both.
context.vcf.reso: The squelch in the filter movement.
context.vcf.envDepth: How far the filter opens with each note. It does not change the sync sweep.
context.porta.time: The slide between notes. The riff has wide jumps, so this is easy to hear.
context.osc.mix: The balance between the plain sawtooth and the synced one.

tweaks.hear: From a slight vowel change at the start of each note to a loud, tearing yelp.
The "yow" slows to a drawn-out "yaaow", and held notes keep changing after they start.
Long, lazy slides, so the line starts to sound like a slide whistle.

sounds.name: Dark Self-Pulsing Echo Drone
sounds.ref: In the style of Brian Eno — "In Dark Trees" ("Another Green World")
sounds.blurb: A low, dark tone that pulses by itself in a steady rhythm, with echoes falling between the pulses.
sounds.how: "In Dark Trees" is a slow, dark piece built on a steady mechanical pulse and deep, echoing tones. Here the keyboard no longer starts the loudness envelope: the square LFO is patched into E.GATE 1, so Envelope 1 fires four times a second on its own and the drone pulses whatever you play. The keys still set the pitch and still trigger Envelope 2, which slowly opens the filter while a note is held. A delay timed to a dotted eighth puts echoes in the gaps, and the sample-and-hold shifts the brightness at random every second or so.

steps.title: A low sawtooth and a pulse below it
steps.why:
A low sawtooth with a pulse an octave below gives a dark, heavy drone. A slight detune makes the two beat slowly.
- SHAPE osc 1 2 (saw), RANGE 16’: the upper voice, an octave below normal.
- SHAPE osc 2 1 (pulse), WIDTH 3 (32%), RANGE 32’: a narrow pulse an octave lower still.
- TUNE osc 2 +0.1 st: very slightly sharp, for the slow beat.
- OSC MIX −1 (60 / 40): the crossfader keeps the saw on top.
- Listen for: a deep, buzzing low note with a slow pulse in its tone.

steps.title: A dark filter that opens slowly on each held note
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) rests dark, and Envelope 2 opens it slowly while a key is held.
- MODE low-pass, FREQ 5.5 (about 560 Hz), RESO 4: dull, with a slight peak.
- KEY TRK off: the cutoff stays put.
- ENV DEPTH 3 (30%): how much brighter the tone gets while a key is held.
- Envelope 2 A 1.2 s, D 1.9 s, S 60%, R 1.1 s: opens over about a second and a half and closes after you let go.
- Listen for: hold a note and hear it slowly open up.

steps.title: Short, plucked loudness
steps.why:
Envelope 1 shapes loudness through the VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier) into a short thump. For now it still fires only when you press a key.
- A 0: instant start.
- D 6 (360 ms), S 0: gone in about a third of a second. Longer decays blur the pulses into a throbbing tone later.
- R 4 (41 ms): a short tail.
- Listen for: one thump per key press.

steps.title: Patch LFO → E.GATE 1
steps.why:
The patch bay lets the LFO (low-frequency oscillator) fire Envelope 1 instead of the keyboard, so the drone pulses by itself.
- LFO → E.GATE 1: replaces the keyboard gate for Envelope 1.
- SHAPE 3 (square): high for half of each cycle, giving one clean trigger per cycle.
- RATE 4.6 (3.99 Hz): about four pulses a second, eighth notes at 120 bpm.
- KEY SYNC on: restarts the LFO on each new note, so the pulse lines up with it.
- Listen for: a steady pulse that carries on after you let go, while the filter closes because Envelope 2 still follows the keys.

steps.title: Patch S&H → FREQ MOD
steps.why:
The S&H (sample and hold) takes a new random value about once a second and nudges the filter with it, so groups of pulses vary in brightness.
- S&H → FREQ MOD: replaces the LFO at the cutoff input.
- MOD DEPTH 1.5 (15%): keeps the random shifts small.
- S&H RATE 3 (1.06 Hz): a new value about every second.
- GLIDE 4 (10 ms): softens the steps slightly.
- Listen for: some runs of pulses a bit brighter or darker than others.

steps.title: Dotted-eighth echoes
steps.why:
A delay timed to a dotted eighth puts echoes between the pulses, and a little overdrive thickens the low end.
- TIME 8.4 (about 370 ms): a dotted eighth at 120 bpm, so each echo falls halfway between two pulses.
- REPEATS 5.5 (55%): several echoes, each duller than the last. Above about 8 they build into a wash.
- MIX 4 (40%): the echoes are clearly heard.
- DRIVE 3, TONE 4.5, LEVEL 8.5: warm grit, slightly dark.
- Listen for: a pulse with a skipping echo rhythm woven between the hits.

context.lfo.rate: In this sound this is the speed of the pulse, because the LFO fires Envelope 1. At 4.6 it is eighth notes at 120 bpm.
context.lfo.shape: Square gives one clean trigger per cycle. Other shapes still cross the gate threshold, but less of each cycle is high.
context.lfo.keySync: Lines the pulse up with the start of each note.
context.env1.d: The length of each pulse. Longer decays blur the pulses into a throbbing tone.
context.env2.a: How slowly the filter opens after you press a key.
context.vcf.envDepth: How much brighter the pulses get while a key is held.
context.vcf.modDepth: How far the sample-and-hold shifts the brightness at random.
context.delay.time: 375 ms, so each echo falls halfway between two pulses.
context.delay.repeats: How many echoes follow each pulse. Above about 8 they build into a steady wash.

tweaks.hear: The pulse slows to under two a second and the echoes become a separate rhythm between them.
Each pulse rings on into the next and the rhythm turns into a slow throb.
The echoes stack up into a dark, churning bed under the pulse.

sounds.name: Swelling Steel-Guitar-Style Lead
sounds.ref: In the style of Daniel Lanois — "Rocco" ("Flesh and Machine")
sounds.blurb: A warm, slow lead in which every note fades in, slides to the next and trails off into long echoes.
sounds.how: Lanois is known for his pedal steel guitar, played with a volume pedal so notes swell in without an attack, and bent up or down into pitch. This patch borrows those two habits. A slow attack on Envelope 1 does the job of the volume pedal, PORTA TIME makes each note slide from the last, and a slight vibrato keeps the held notes alive. A long delay with plenty of repeats washes the notes into one another.

steps.title: A warm blend of sawtooth and triangle
steps.why:
A warm blend of saw and triangle gives a tone with some edge but no buzz, like a steel guitar through a clean amplifier.
- SHAPE osc 1 2.6 (saw towards triangle): some edge. Towards saw is brighter, more like an overdriven steel.
- SHAPE osc 2 3 (triangle), TUNE +0.1 st: a triangle a few cents sharp, for slow beating.
- RANGE 8’ on both, OSC MIX 0 (50 / 50): same octave, equal blend on the crossfader.
- Listen for: a warm, slightly shimmering tone.

steps.title: A soft filter that follows the keys
steps.why:
The VCF (voltage-controlled filter) softens the top and follows the keys. Brightness stays fixed within each note; only loudness will move.
- MODE low-pass, FREQ 6.8 (about 1.4 kHz): how warm or bright the tone is.
- RESO 2: resonance, a small edge at the cutoff.
- KEY TRK on: key tracking keeps higher notes from going dull.
- ENV DEPTH 0: no envelope moves the cutoff.
- Listen for: a softer, rounder tone than before.

steps.title: The volume-pedal swell
steps.why:
Envelope 1 shapes loudness through the VCA (voltage-controlled amplifier). A slow attack does the job of a steel player’s volume pedal: notes rise out of nothing with no pick sound.
- A 7.6 (480 ms): about half a second to swell in. At 5 it starts more like a plucked string.
- D 820 ms, S 100%: full level held.
- R 8 (1.1 s): about a second of fade after you let go.
- Listen for: each note rising gently into place.

steps.title: Bends between notes
steps.why:
Portamento bends each note in from the last. Because the swell is slow, the slide happens while the note is still quiet, like a steel bar sliding into place.
- PORTA TIME 2 (400 ms): about 0.4 seconds per slide. At 0 notes step; above 3 the slides sound seasick.
- Listen for: notes arriving in pitch as they get louder.

steps.title: Patch ATT 2 → OSC 1+2 for a slight vibrato
steps.why:
Attenuator 2 already carries the LFO (low-frequency oscillator, a slow wave that moves other settings). This cable adds it to both oscillators’ pitch for a slow hand vibrato.
- ATT 2 → OSC 1+2: the LFO to both pitches. The pulse-width feed does nothing, as neither oscillator is on a pulse shape.
- 2 at 0.7: about a quarter of a semitone. Above about 1.5 it sounds out of tune.
- RATE 4.6 (3.99 Hz), SHAPE sine, KEY SYNC off: about 4 Hz, smooth and free-running.
- Listen for: held notes wavering slowly.

steps.title: Long, washed echoes
steps.why:
A long delay with plenty of repeats washes the notes into one another, and a little overdrive warms the tone.
- TIME 9 (460 ms): a long gap between echoes.
- REPEATS 6.5 (65%): each note keeps coming back for several seconds. Above about 9 they stop dying away.
- MIX 4.5 (45%): echoes nearly level with the dry note.
- DRIVE 1.5, TONE 4, LEVEL 8: gentle warmth, slightly dark.
- Listen for: old notes sinking behind new ones, each repeat a little duller.

context.env1.a: In this sound this is the volume pedal. At 7.6 each note takes about half a second to swell in; at 5 it starts more like a plucked string.
context.porta.time: The bend into each note. At 0 the notes step; above 3 the slides are slow enough to sound seasick.
context.att.2: The vibrato depth. Keep it small: above about 1.5 it sounds out of tune.
context.lfo.rate: The vibrato speed, about 4 Hz.
context.delay.repeats: How long the echoes last. Above about 9 they stop dying away.
context.delay.mix: How loud the echoes are against the dry note.
context.vcf.freq: How warm or bright the tone is.
context.osc1.shape: Between sawtooth and triangle. Towards sawtooth is brighter and more like an overdriven steel.

tweaks.hear: From a plucked note with a soft front to a slow swell that barely arrives before the next note.
Each note bends in from further away, closer to a slow steel-guitar slide.
The echoes pile up into a sustained chord under the melody.
